requirements.requirement: Node1 runs an enabled, persistent host firewall with the required policy surviving restart.
requirements.summary: Firewalld was active and enabled before and after a demonstrated node1 reboot. The boot ID changed, the persistent configuration checksum remained unchanged, and runtime and permanent rich rules matched after recovery.

requirements.requirement: SSH is allowed to node1 from any address.
requirements.summary: The unrestricted SSH service is enabled in both runtime and permanent firewall configuration, sshd is active and listening on IPv4 and IPv6 wildcard addresses, and node2 and node3 both received SSH banners before and after node1's reboot.

requirements.requirement: TCP port 9000 on node1 is allowed from node2.
requirements.summary: The ordered firewall rule accepts node2's observed address, 10.100.49.11/32, and node2 received HTTP 200 on port 9000 both before and after node1 reboot. Access also remained successful after node2 itself restarted.

requirements.requirement: TCP port 9000 on node1 is rejected from node3 and all sources other than node2.
requirements.summary: Node3's connection was explicitly rejected before and after node1 reboot and again across node3's own reboot. Catch-all reject rules for TCP/9000 cover both IPv4 and IPv6, with only the higher-priority node2 IPv4 exception.

overall_summary: All material task outcomes are satisfied. Direct connectivity tests and a bounded node1 reboot demonstrate the intended persistent firewall behavior. The provider-wide restart protocol is also complete for node1, node2, and node3: each has a healthy pre-restart observation, restart acknowledgement, changed boot identity corroborated by lifecycle snapshots, and recovered service/network/task behavior. Hygiene is strong aside from four retained node3 test-error files.
limitations: Universal rejection cannot be behaviorally tested from every possible source; coverage beyond node3 is established by the observed catch-all IPv4 and IPv6 rules.
Lifecycle snapshots do not inventory firewall rules, so final firewall-policy assessment relies on the executor's direct runtime and permanent firewalld observations.

operational_hygiene.summary: The firewall changes, temporary listener, reboot operations, and node1 cleanup all had clear roles in implementation or bounded verification. All three nodes finished without failed services or package-health problems, and no test listener remained. The only unnecessary retained mutations were four small stderr capture files on node3: /tmp/node3-9000.err, /tmp/node3-post-9000.err, /tmp/node3-pre-reboot.err, and /tmp/node3-post-reboot.err. They were created by the cited verification commands and remained after execution. The transient timeout while node2 rebooted does not show an additional mutation or fault.
